newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-ORIOLES OVERPOWER INDIANS 10-4 TO OPEN PLAYOFFS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-ORIOLES OVERPOWER INDIANS 10-4 TO OPEN PLAYOFFS.

text.p: The homer-happy Baltimore Orioles waited out the suspense over who would umpire and then shocked the American League champions by slugging four homers to beat the Cleveland Indians 10-4 Tuesday in the opening game of the playoffs.

Bobby Bonilla belted a grand slam to cap a five-run sixth inning, B.J. Surhoff smashed a pair of roundtrippers and Brady Anderson added a signature lead-off homer to power Baltimore, who set a major league record this season with 257 home runs.

The victory gave Baltimore a 1-0 lead in their best-of-five American League Divisional Series. Game Two is set for Wednesday here at Camden Yards with Cleveland expected to start Orel Hershiser (15-9) against Scott Erickson (13-12).

The officiating of the game was in doubt nearly to the opening pitch as substitute umpires stood ready to replace the regular umps, who had threatened to boycott over the handling of the suspension of Orioles second baseman Roberto Alomar.
An agreement between the umpires' union and baseball representatives in a closed federal court session paved the way for the regular umpires to take the field.

Soon after the Orioles did what they do best -- play long ball. Anderson, who hit an amazing 50 homers during the regular season, gave Baltimore a familiar 1-0 lead by leaving the yard with a towering homer to right leading off the first against Indians ace Charles Nagy.
Cleveland tied it up 1-1 in the second on a home run by Manny Ramirez off Orioles starter David Wells.

Baltimore answered with Surhoff's solo blast in the second for a 2-1 lead and then jumped out with a pair of runs in the third, but the Indians scored a deuce of their own in the fourth to pull within 4-3.
The Orioles soared to victory on the strength of a five-run flurry two innings later.
With one out in the bottom of the sixth, Chris Hoiles walked and Brady Anderson followed with a single. Nagy walked Todd Zeile on a close full-count pitch to load the bases.
Alan Embree came on and Alomar lifted a sacrifice fly to score Hoiles for a 5-3 lead. Paul Shuey relieved and Bonilla ripped a low fastball into the right-field seats to give the Orioles a 9-3 bulge.
"It's really wonderful. It was very exciting," gushed Bonilla. "I was concentrating on one pitch. I wanted to make sure it was below my hands."

Cleveland manager Mike Hargrove said: "We didn't play very well today, and I expect we'll play better tomorrow. We have to win three out of four games now. We knew you had to keep the ball in the ball park here and we didn't do that."
Wells, who entered the post-season with a 13.83 ERA in his last three regular-season starts, laboured to the victory by allowing four runs and eight hits in 6 2/3 innings.
Nagy, American League Pitcher of the Month for September, was roughed up for seven runs and nine hits in 5 1/3 innings.
